title: UK domestic-electricity VAT reverts 0% to 5% in Great Britain (SI 2026/987 lapses 31 March 2027) — the drag drops out of April's CPI, and a second, larger base effect lands in October 2027
source: NEWS: THE PREFIX IS A TAXONOMY ARTIFACT, NOT A DOUBT ABOUT THE MECHANISM — THE SUNSET IS INSIDE THE INSTRUMENT. Primary, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200): legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/987/made, The Value Added Tax (Supplies of Domestic Electricity) Order 2026, made 2026-09-07 and laid 2026-09-08, has effect only for supplies made in the period 'beginning with 1st October 2026 and ending with 31st March 2027' — no further act is required for the 5% reduced rate to resume on 1 April 2027. Corroborated the same session from three further primaries fetched direct: (1) HMRC's tax information and impact note (gov.uk content API, first published 2026-09-08T17:00:05+01:00), which budgets approximately 100 electricity suppliers for 'updating systems again to change the rate from 0% to 5% when the temporary zero rate comes to an end on 31 March 2027'; (2) Revenue and Customs Brief 10 (2026), which states 'The temporary zero rate applies from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027'; (3) the 21 July 2026 gov.uk announcement, which costs the relief at 'around GBP 850 million in 2026-27' — a costing scoped to the financial year that ends on the lapse date, i.e. one that books no extension. Filed estimate on two honest counts: the date is contingent on the Order NOT being extended by a fresh statutory instrument before 2027-03-31 (the government's own words are 'Any further action, including on funding for longer-term measures, will be taken at the Budget alongside an OBR forecast', 21 July 2026 — narrower than the press gloss that an extension 'will be considered'), and market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for legislation.gov.uk, HMRC or ONS. Proposed 2026-09-09 by the uk-electricity-vat-zero-rate-2026-10-01 lane; researched and made canonical by its own lane the same day
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THE never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-09, superseding proposals/uk-electricity-vat-reversion-2027-04-01.from-uk-electricity-vat-zero-rate-2026-10-01.json (read in full first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md). The proposer's placement finding stands and its structural point survives: the half of a self-reversing tax notch that nobody diarises is the half that gets misread. WHAT THE INITIAL RESEARCH CHANGED, AND IT IS THE POINT: THE PROPOSAL SAID 'THE SAME -0.10pp, BACK THE OTHER WAY'. THE CONCLUSION IS RIGHT AND THE REASON GIVEN FOR IT IS WRONG, AND TWO ERRORS CANCEL. Naive reversion arithmetic is NOT symmetric -- removing 5% VAT cuts a VAT-inclusive price by 5/105 = 4.7619%, but restoring it RAISES the (now VAT-free) price by 5/100 = 5.0%, which is 5% MORE than the cut took out. What offsets it is ONS's own weight convention: per the published updating-weights methodology (fetched 2026-09-09), the weights applied in year Y are expenditure price-updated to December Y-1 for the January index and to January Y thereafter -- and BOTH December 2026 and January 2027 fall INSIDE the zero-rate window, so the 2027 CPI electricity weight is price-updated through a VAT-free electricity price and is mechanically about 1/1.05 of its counterfactual. (1/1.05) x (5/100) = 5/105 EXACTLY. The symmetry is real; it is an artifact of the weighting convention, not of the tax arithmetic. WHAT DOES NOT CANCEL IS THE WEIGHT VINTAGE: the cut used the published 2026 weight (ONS series CJXA, 20.6065 per 1000, fetched 2026-09-09) but the reversion uses the 2027 weight, unknown until the January 2027 index publishes on 2027-02-17, drawn from 2025 expenditure. CJXA's own recent history is volatile -- 27.0 (2023), 23.3142 (2024), 19.1488 (2025), 20.6065 (2026) -- which maps the April 2027 step to a range of roughly 0.091pp to 0.129pp, centred near 0.098pp. THE FINDING WORTH THE MOST: THERE ARE FOUR DATED VAT STEPS IN THE UK CPI YEAR-ON-YEAR PATH, NOT TWO. The drag appears in the October 2026 print (-0.10pp), persists to March 2027, DROPS OUT in the April 2027 print (published 2027-05-19, ONS release calendar fetched -- a hot April UK print is arithmetic, not re-acceleration), and then a SECOND, UPWARD base effect APPEARS in the October 2027 print (published 2027-11-17) and runs to March 2028, because that print compares a normal-rated month against a zero-rated base. The October 2027 step is the one nobody has diarised; both venues are proposed in the same PR. PROCEDURE, CORRECTED: extension is CHEAPER than the proposer implied. An early repeal would be caught by VATA 1994 s.97(4)(c)(iii) and need an affirmative Commons vote, but an EXTENSION creates or continues a zero-rated group and is therefore NOT caught -- a fresh negative-procedure SI, layable at any time up to 2027-03-31, no vote required. Cheap to start, cheap to extend, cheap to lapse, expensive only to end early. The near-term procedural clock is the annulment window on SI 2026/987: 40 days from laying under Statutory Instruments Act 1946 s.5 (fetched), not the 28 days of VATA s.97(3), which is the made-affirmative approval clock for a different class of order. PASS-THROUGH IS PERMITTED, NOT FORCED, ON THE WAY BACK UP: Ofgem's 2026-08-26 cap release (fetched) says 'VAT is not included in electricity bills for people covered under the energy price cap between 1 October and 31 December 2026' -- the cap is a VAT-inclusive maximum, so it FORCED the cut through; on reversion the April-June 2027 cap (announced on the quarterly cadence, roughly late February 2027, from Ofgem's own 'next announcement 25 November 2026' for the January-March cap) simply rises, which permits rather than compels the increase. Tiered LOW: symbols: [], and the calendar's entire tracked universe is eight US mega-caps with no UK listing, utility, gilt or sterling leg. Note the same-date collision worth keeping straight: japan-food-tax-cut-2027-04-01 is a SECOND mechanical consumption-tax notch on 2027-04-01, in the OPPOSITE direction and roughly ten times the size, in a different national CPI. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this. Ledger: docs/research/events/uk-electricity-vat-reversion-2027-04-01.md
